_comment: Backup verification -- watches directories where scheduled backup jobs are expected to drop dated files, and reports two DELIBERATELY SEPARATE real signals per target: how long since the newest matching file landed ('the job stopped running'), and how big that newest file actually is ('the job ran but wrote something suspiciously tiny/empty'). Copy to config/backup_targets.json and point at real backup drop locations -- this collector is skipped entirely if that file doesn't exist, same as cert_targets.json/software_versions.json. Does NOT verify backup file CONTENT integrity (never opens/extracts/restores the file to confirm it isn't corrupt) -- only that a recent, non-tiny file landed where expected; see collectors/backup_verification.py's module docstring for why that's a deliberate v1 scope limit, not an oversight. expected_max_age_hours/min_expected_size_bytes below are informational only -- this collector does not read them at collection time (build_thresholds() has no per-entry lookup into a collector's own manifest), they're here so the operator has the real expected numbers on hand when writing THIS target's own threshold rule into config/thresholds_config.py.

targets._note: nightly full DB dump onto a local disk -- expected every night, so the generic thresholds_config.py default (stress at 30h, critical at 48h) is a reasonable fit as-is
targets.name: practice-db-nightly

targets._note: weekly compressed image backup onto a network share -- note the much longer expected_max_age_hours than the nightly target above; the generic default in thresholds_config.py would false-alarm on this one every week, real reason this collector doesn't try to auto-enforce one global age threshold and expects a per-target override here instead
targets.name: imaging-server-weekly

targets._note: nightly config/settings export -- a small file is NORMAL here, deliberately a much lower min_expected_size_bytes than the DB dump above; real illustration of why this collector ships no generic default size threshold at all
targets.name: config-export-nightly
